title: Geometric coherence of normalized continuous coefficients
statement: Let D be a finite field datum and l a prime. For any family c assigning CoefficientFamily l E to each finite normed Q_l-extension E [def-zl-continuous-constructible-lattice-data], there exists CoefficientGeometry D l c. It consists of normalized integral and rational isomorphisms for locally closed immersions of separated finite-type D.k-schemes, their inverse-image composition equations, finite coefficient embeddings with their integer maps and compatible quotient-power reductions, and commutation of coefficient embeddings with restriction and with composition. This is coefficient data alone, with no constructible module or lattice.

proof.text: First check the geometric hypotheses for every scheme to which the coefficient and lattice results will be applied. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and itself, and its spectrum is a quasi-compact single affine open; thus the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma makes $W$ and $T$ Noetherian. The closed-subsets-minimal lemma gives their Noetherian underlying spaces. Every subspace of a Noetherian space is Noetherian: an ascending chain of relative opens lifts to an ascending chain of ambient opens by taking successive unions. Thus a locally closed subscheme $S$ has quasi-compact underlying space, as do its opens. Its immersion is locally of finite type by the immersion lemma and its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by permanence. Consequently $S$ is finite type over $k$: the source is quasi-compact and the target has one point. It is locally Noetherian by the locally-finite-type lemma and hence Noetherian. An immersion is separated (its relative diagonal is an isomorphism), so permanence also makes $S/k$ separated. These observations apply to successive strata and their reductions.

For a locally closed $h:Z\to W$, use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms of the immersion-coefficients theorem. The scheme-naturality lemma says that the condensed chart and the continuous chart commute with the actual pullback maps. Inverse-image composition and coefficient postcomposition commute by the coefficient-pullback-composition lemma, so successive restrictions give the same comparison. On each quotient, the integral comparison of step 2 is reduction; after localization it is the map induced by that reduction. For a finite coefficient extension $E\subset E'$, naturality of the chart in the continuous maps $A\to A'$ and $E\to E'$ gives the extension square as well. Quotients are compared whenever the map descends to the chosen ideals, equivalently after passing to a cofinal compatible pair of uniformizer powers in a ramified extension. Each such comparison sends the residue class of $a$ to the residue class of its image. Equality on these projections proves equality on the limit; equality on coefficients and the inverted uniformizer proves equality on localization. Tensor comparisons are the balanced maps described next.
